h1: The 5 Best Makita Leaf Blowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Makita Leaf Blowers 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 5 Makita cordless leaf blowers scored on airflow, 18V and 36V (18V x2) power, kit contents and battery platform value.
summary: The Makita XBU03SM1 kit is the one to buy if you do not own LXT batteries: 459 CFM, brushless, and ready to run from the box. Already own 18V LXT packs? The bare XBU03Z gets you the same blower for much less. For the most air, the XBU02PT 36V kit reaches 473 CFM on two batteries. The DUB185Z is the budget handheld for light yard work.
intro: Buying a Makita blower is really buying into a battery platform. The 18V LXT system powers hundreds of tools, so the cheapest way to own a Makita blower is often a bare tool that borrows batteries from your drill or saw. Pay for a kit when you already have those packs and you have paid twice for the same thing.

We ranked five Makita cordless blowers on the Primea framework, weighting airflow, platform value and what is actually in the box. They split into three groups: single-battery 18V blowers, two-battery 36V (18V x2) blowers, and one older handheld. Any non-Makita blowers were excluded so this reads as a pure Makita comparison.

products.name: Makita XBU03SM1 18V LXT® Lithium-Ion Brushless Cordless Blower Kit
products.verdict: The 459 CFM brushless blower with a battery in the box. The easiest Makita to own.
products.description:
This kit pairs the 18V LXT brushless blower, rated at 459 CFM, with the battery and charger needed to run it. Brushless motors waste less energy as heat, which stretches a charge and lengthens the motor's life against brushed rivals.

It outranks the bare XBU03Z only because it works the day it arrives. The blower is identical, so the extra cost is purely for the battery and charger. It trails the 36V XBU02PT on peak airflow, but one battery is lighter to carry than two.

Buy it if you have no Makita batteries and want the lightest full-power option. The caveat: single 18V packs set the runtime ceiling, so large yards may need a second pack.
pros: Ready to use out of box
cons: Kit costs more than bare tool
products.idealFor: Homeowners who do not yet own Makita LXT batteries.
products.skipIf: You already own several 18V LXT batteries and a charger.

products.name: Makita XBU03Z 18V LXT® Lithium-Ion Brushless Cordless Blower
products.verdict: The same 459 CFM blower, sold bare. The smart buy if you already own LXT packs.
products.description:
The XBU03Z is the tool-only version of the XBU03SM1, so it carries the same 18V LXT brushless motor and 459 CFM rating. The Z suffix in Makita part numbers marks a bare tool, with no battery or charger included.

It ranks second because the kit saves a beginner a separate battery purchase and avoids the compatibility question. For anyone already on LXT, though, this is the better value, since you skip paying for a second charger and pack.

Right for people with a drill, saw or trimmer on the same system. The caveat is that this listing will not run on its own, and buyers who miss the bare-tool wording often send it back unopened.
products.idealFor: Anyone with existing 18V LXT batteries and a charger.
products.skipIf: You own no Makita batteries at all.

products.name: Makita XBU02PT 36V (18V X2) LXT® Brushless Blower Kit
products.verdict: 473 CFM from two 18V batteries working as one 36V pack. The strongest Makita here.
products.description:
This kit runs on two 18V LXT batteries together, which Makita labels 36V (18V X2), and it is rated at 473 CFM, the highest airflow among the five. Doubling the batteries raises available power without moving to a separate 36V platform.

It lands third because the lead over the 459 CFM XBU03SM1 is only 14 CFM on paper, while a second battery adds weight and expense. That small gap is the honest case against paying for the dual-battery design.

A fit for large yards and heavy, wet fall leaf loads where the second pack doubles runtime. The caveat is bulk: two batteries sit on the tool, and you need both charged before every session.
cons: Kit costs the most to start
products.idealFor: Large yards and heavy, wet autumn leaf loads.
products.skipIf: A single-battery blower already covers your yard.

products.name: Makita XBU02Z 36V (18V X2) LXT® Brushless Blower
products.verdict: The tool-only 36V blower. Cheap entry if you already hold four spare LXT packs.
products.description:
The XBU02Z is the bare-tool version of the dual-battery 36V (18V X2) design, so it needs two LXT batteries to run. It uses the same brushless architecture as the kit above and sits in the $200 to $500 price tier.

It ranks below the XBU02PT kit because the kit gives you the airflow and the power source together, while this listing leaves you shopping for two compatible batteries and a charger. The saving only appears if those packs are already in the garage.

Best for professionals or heavy LXT users who run many tools from the same pool of batteries. The caveat: our facts do not state an airflow figure for this exact listing, so check it before comparing it with the kit.
products.idealFor: Heavy LXT users who already own several spare batteries.
products.skipIf: You would be buying two batteries just for this blower.

products.name: Makita DUB185Z Cordless Handheld Leaf Blower Powered by 18V LXT
products.verdict: A simple handheld on the 18V LXT platform. Cheapest in the group, lightest on specs.
products.description:
The DUB185Z is a handheld cordless blower powered by a single 18V LXT battery, listed in the $50 to $100 tier. It is the cheapest Makita here and a straightforward tool for patios, steps and small lawns.

It ranks last because Makita's own listing gives no brushless claim or CFM figure here, while both XBU03 models state 459 CFM and a brushless motor. You are buying simplicity and price, not power.

A sound add-on for an LXT owner who wants something light for sweeping decks. The caveat is that, with no airflow number to check, it is hard to promise it will move wet or matted leaves.
products.idealFor: LXT owners who want a light blower for hard surfaces.
products.skipIf: You need to move wet leaves across a full lawn.

methodology.title: Airflow rating
methodology.description: Stated CFM decided the order wherever Makita published it, and unpublished figures counted against a model.

methodology.title: Motor technology
methodology.description: Brushless models ranked above listings that did not state a motor type, because brushless motors run cooler and last longer.

methodology.title: Battery platform value
methodology.description: We scored how much of the cost goes to the blower versus batteries, since LXT owners need a very different purchase than newcomers.

methodology.title: What is in the box
methodology.description: Kits with battery and charger were rated against bare tools by who benefits, not simply by cost.

methodology.title: Runtime and weight
methodology.description: Single-battery 18V designs were credited for lighter carry, and dual-battery 36V designs for longer sessions.

whatMatters.detail: Makita sells most tools two ways. A Z suffix means the tool alone, with no battery or charger. A kit includes them. If you already own LXT batteries, bare is far cheaper. If you do not, the kit is the true price. Read the title and the in-the-box list before you add to the cart.

The 36V models use two 18V LXT batteries side by side, not a separate battery. That doubles available energy for more airflow and runtime. It also doubles the weight on the tool and the charging effort. Check how many batteries the listing says are needed.

Without carbon brushes rubbing on the rotor, this motor sheds less heat, so it gets more work from each charge and ages slower. Both XBU03 listings state it. When a listing like the DUB185Z does not, assume you are paying for the cheaper construction.

CFM is the air volume the blower moves each minute, and it is the best indicator of how much debris a blower can shift. Compare it only between models that publish it. Here the 459 CFM and 473 CFM models are close, so battery cost, not airflow, should decide.

LXT batteries work across Makita's drills, saws, trimmers and more, so a blower on that platform costs less if you own any of them. Check which tools you have before buying. The reverse is also true: the blower pulls you toward buying more LXT tools later.

faq.q: Will the Makita XBU03Z run without a battery?
faq.a: No. The Z suffix means tool only. It needs an 18V LXT battery and charger, which come with the XBU03SM1 kit. If you own an LXT drill or saw, those batteries fit the XBU03Z directly.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake buying a Makita blower?
faq.a: Ordering a bare tool by accident. The XBU03Z and XBU03SM1 look nearly identical in the search results, but only the kit includes power. Check the title for the word kit before you buy.

faq.q: Is the 36V XBU02PT worth it over the 18V XBU03SM1?
faq.a: Rarely. The XBU02PT is rated at 473 CFM against 459 CFM for the XBU03SM1, a small gap, and it needs two batteries. Choose it only for large yards where doubled runtime matters more than weight.

The tool takes two 18V LXT batteries at the same time and combines them, so no separate 36V battery exists. The XBU02Z and XBU02PT both work this way, and you need two charged packs before each session.

faq.q: How should I look after the battery?
faq.a: Store LXT packs at room temperature, off the charger once full, and out of a freezing garage. With the XBU02PT kit, rotate which battery sits in which slot so both wear evenly over time.

faq.q: Can the DUB185Z handle wet leaves?
faq.a: Probably not well. The listing gives no CFM figure, while the XBU03Z states 459 CFM. Treat the DUB185Z as a sweeper for decks, steps and dry debris, and use an XBU03 model for lawn leaf piles.

finalTake: Most buyers should get the Makita XBU03SM1 kit: 459 CFM, brushless, and the battery is in the box. If you own LXT packs, save money and take the bare XBU03Z. Reserve the XBU02PT for big, leaf-heavy lots, and use the DUB185Z only where a light handheld sweeper is enough. Whatever you buy, the real purchase is the battery platform.
